auth_methods.quote: DealCloud uses the OAuth2 Client Credentials flow to generate a bearer token
auth_methods.note: Per-user API key (enabled in profile) is exchanged for a 15-minute OAuth2 bearer token. MCP uses interactive OAuth 2.0 per user.

credential_access.note: Two readings. (1) admin_approval: API access needs a user in a group with the 'API' capability enabled by a site admin, then the user enables their API key in Profile. (2) contact_sales: DealCloud is an enterprise product with no public trial/pricing/self-serve signup, so a developer without a licensed tenant cannot obtain credentials at all. Best guess: admin_approval (given the access path is tenant-admin controlled).

production_gate.quote: To enable API access, ensure the intended user is assigned to a user group with the appropriate permissions.
production_gate.note: Per-tenant credentials; no app review, marketplace or partner agreement found in the public API docs (absence of evidence).

api_type.quote: This site provides a comprehensive overview of our REST APIs, their capabilities, and available endpoints.
api_type.note: Also SDKs and MCP server, but the API itself is REST/Swagger.

mcp_official.quote: The DealCloud MCP Server helps teams turn their DealCloud data into faster, higher-quality outcomes.

main_blocker_type.quote: If you do not see the Admin section, contact your organization's admin or DealCloud Customer Success Manager (CSM) for assistance.
main_blocker_type.note: Customer/tenant-gated; no public sandbox or self-serve path.
